title: ShippedPost
description: What somebody built, written so another builder would want to look. Every sentence describes work that is actually in the input: a technology the work never used, or a feature nothing shows, is the worst thing this document can contain, because it is a public claim the reader has no way to check.

what.description: one line: what this is. Written for somebody who has never seen the project. Not the repo name, not a commit message, no jargon a non-programmer would miss. (max 100 chars)

why.description: who it is for and what it lets them do, in one sentence. Null when the work genuinely does not say, which is better than a guess. (max 200 chars)

stage.description: how far along it is, from what the work shows. Tests and commits say working; a first scaffold says prototype.

changes.description: what is new since last time, each a thing somebody could try. Never a list of files touched. (1 to 4 items)

hard_part.description: the thing that was genuinely difficult, and what it turned out to be. THE FIELD THIS SPEC EXISTS FOR. Grounded in the evidence you were given, never invented. Null when nothing in the work was hard, which is a real answer. (max 400 chars)

stack.description: technologies actually visible in the work. Never inferred from the kind of project it looks like. (each max 60 chars, max 6 items)

demo.description: the one screenshot or clip that would show this off, named concretely. Null when there is nothing visual to show. (max 200 chars)

next.description: what is obviously next, only when the work itself says so (a TODO, a failing test left in, a stated intent). Null otherwise. (max 200 chars)

text.description: one thing that is now possible that was not before, in plain words. Not a commit message, not a file name. (max 200 chars)

evidence.description: what in the work shows it: a commit, a test, a number the input gave you. Null when the input only described it. (max 200 chars)
